To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the heritability for heart rate ratio was 0,43 and the heritabilities for the blood gas parameters measured at 3 wk were low (0.02 for partial pressure of carbon-dioxide in venous blood; 0.03 partial pressure of oxygen and blood oxygen saturation; 0.15 for pH; 0.19 for bicarbonate and total carbon dioxide).
blood gas parameters do not seem to be useful for the genetic improvement of ascites susceptibility in broiler chickens.

the heritability for heart weight ratio was moderate (0.43 +/- 0.12) and that the genetic correlations between heart weight ratio and blood gas parameters were low and close to zero, except for the genetic correlation between heart weight ratio with pvO(2) (-0.62).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and phenotypical relationships between blood gas measurements, the heart ratio, and body weight in broilers.
the genetic relationships between blood gas traits, ascites, and BW at different ages.
the development of a selection program against ascites susceptibility in broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
blood gas parameters have only a limited potential to be used as indicator traits in ascites selection programs.
the genetic correlations between heart rate and blood gas parameters are not sufficiently strong to use the latter as indicator traits for the selection against ascites.
blood gas parameters are not useful traits to select for or against ascites susceptibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heart ratio is a good trait to use to select against ascites, whereas the blood gas parameters are not.
the genetic correlation between blood gas parameters measured in wk 3 or wk 4 and the heart ratio is not strong enough to be useful for the improvement of ascites susceptibility in broilers.
the heart ratio is a good indicator trait for ascites and that the heart ratio can be measured in an easy and reliable way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic correlation between the heart ratio and pvO(2) is negative and strong and that the heart ratio and blood oxygen saturation are positively correlated.
the heart ratio can be used to estimate genetic merit for ascites susceptibility and to improve ascites resistance.
the heart ratio is a reliable and easy-to-mease postmortem indicator for susceptibility of broilers to ascites.
